rationale.edition: All three changed files live under web/src/lib/vue-shortcut-manager/ — the open-source frontend. No path touches enterprise/, o2_enterprise/, or any enterprise-owned module. Enterprise keywords (cipherKeys, rbac, onlineEvals, nodes) appear only as gating metadata the OSS cheatsheet reads to hide enterprise pages on OSS builds; they do not move the change into an enterprise path.
rationale.skip: Not skipped. There is no tests-added label or skip comment, and the change alters a user-facing UI (the keyboard shortcut cheatsheet dialog) rather than docs/CI/comment content.
rationale.e2e: E2E is warranted. ShortcutCheatsheet.vue is a user-visible dialog, and the change filters which pages and module chips it lists based on edition (config.isEnterprise / isCloud) and /config flags (rbac_enabled, online_evals_enabled, incidents_enabled, model_pricing_enabled). The user-visible behavior that needs verifying is that an OSS build no longer lists enterprise/cloud-only pages while the enterprise build still does.
rationale.area: The change lives in web/src/lib/vue-shortcut-manager/ — a global UI library, not a Logs/Metrics/Dashboards feature. GeneralTests is the closest fit for cross-cutting UI behavior and is where sibling global specs (sanity, enrichment, theme-management, cipherKeys) live.
rationale.group: GeneralTests — the existing matrix shard (testfolder 'GeneralTests', actual_folder 'GeneralTests') whose run_files already host cross-cutting UI specs, so the new spec belongs there.
rationale.existing_tests: No E2E specs in the diff. The only test added is web/src/lib/vue-shortcut-manager/__tests__/shortcutRegistry.spec.ts, a Vitest unit test, not a Playwright E2E spec, so it does not count as existing E2E coverage.
